chunks: ʿAlī ibn Mahzīyār, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Is ghusl obligatory upon the one who washes the dead body? He said: “Yes.” I said: Then if he touches it while it is still warm? He said: “There is no ghusl upon him; but when it becomes cold, then ghusl is upon him.” I said: And [regarding] beasts and birds, if he touches them, is ghusl upon him? He said: “No, this is not like the human being.”

key_terms.سُخْنٌ: still warm, before the body has cooled
key_terms.غُسْلٌ: ritual bath made obligatory in this context
key_terms.مَسَّهُ: touched him, meaning the dead body

ai.seo_question: Is ghusl required after washing or touching a dead body in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about ghusl connected to contact with a dead human body. It states that ghusl applies to the one who washes or touches the corpse after it has become cold, while touching dead animals or birds does not carry the same ruling.
